notes:
Two new switches at the bottom of the front page. Both are off until you turn them on, so if you ignore them this version farms exactly like 4.7.

TURN THE SCREEN DOWN

Nobody is watching the phone play, and the screen is one of the biggest sources of heat and battery drain on it. With this switched on, the brightness drops to about five percent the moment farming starts, and goes back to exactly what it was - including whether automatic brightness was on - when you stop.

It also goes back to normal the instant you open MW AFK, so picking the phone up never hands you a dark screen you have to fight.

The first time you turn it on, Android will ask for permission, because brightness is one of its own settings rather than one of ours. The switch takes you straight to the right screen: tap Allow modifying system settings, then come back. Once only, on the phone, no cable needed.

If the app is ever killed outright while the screen is down, opening it again puts the brightness back. There is no way to end up with a phone stuck dark.

Why it changes the real brightness rather than drawing something dark over the screen: the macro watches the screen through the same mirror that would show it our dark layer. A dark layer would have dimmed every picture it has to recognise and broken every rule in it. The backlight is invisible to it.

ONLY FARM BETWEEN SET TIMES

Off means it farms for as long as you leave it running, which is what it has always done. Switch it on and you pick a start time and a stop time.

Outside those hours it waits. The badge at the top says WAITING in amber and the app tells you what time it is waiting for, instead of saying RUNNING while nothing happens.

It waits rather than stopping, on purpose. Android only hands over permission to watch the screen when a person taps its dialog, so a macro that stopped itself at six in the morning could not start itself again at ten at night without somebody standing there. Waiting costs nothing and picks up on its own.

The screen stays dimmed through the wait, since the game keeps the phone awake either way.

ALSO IN THIS VERSION

Fixed before it shipped: opening the app counted as flipping the new switches, which would have re-opened Android permission screen on every launch.

Three things were considered and deliberately left out rather than forgotten: pausing when the phone gets hot, stopping before the battery runs down, and skipping the aircraft slots that are empty. The last one because those taps happen during a battle, where they cost nothing.
